title: The Thorns That Grow Back
story: Glasswort the Thorn Golem blocks the crystal cavern where three lost cave-mappers are sheltering, and it bristles with 33 razor-sharp crystal thorns. Each sweep of Mr 6's sword shears off 5 thorns — but if even one thorn remains afterward, 3 more chime into place. Mr 6 sits down on a rock and thinks it all the way through before swinging once.
question: Starting from 33 thorns, if each sweep removes 5 and then 3 regrow whenever at least one thorn is left, how many sweeps does Mr 6 need to clear every thorn?
hint: Each ordinary sweep only nets a loss of 2 thorns — but think about the final sweep, when 5 or fewer are left and nothing can grow back.
victory: On the fifteenth sweep the last five thorns rang like wind chimes and Glasswort shrank into a friendly little quartz pebble. Mr 6 pocketed it and walked the mappers home. 'The trick,' he said, 'was counting the last swing separately.'
imagePrompt: A towering golem of jagged clear crystal thorns blocking a glittering cave mouth, a numeral-six knight mid-swing with light refracting into rainbows across the walls.
solution: A normal sweep removes 5 but 3 regrow, so the net loss is 5 - 3 = 2 thorns.
The 15th sweep removes those last 5 with nothing left to regrow, so Mr 6 needs 15 sweeps.
praise: Using the net loss of 2 per sweep was exactly the right idea — the final sweep just works differently because nothing regrows.
